Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

agree verb

to a plan, on terms

also agreed!, come to an agreement, okay, OK, all right, fine, OK then, okay then, alright, alright then, I have no objection, no objection, fine by me, granted

classical

Plaut. Capt. 378
Cic. Att. 6.1.14 (Lewis & Short)

convenit (inter nōs)

impersonal use of conveniō: mihi cum aliquō, or inter aliquōs; with ut and the subjunctive

it is agreed (between us); we agree on

Other words

  • Fīat. — Agreed! All right

    verb: present subjunctive of fīō, “let it be done” · also used · classical · Ter. Ph. 1054; Plaut. Asin. 40; Traupman 110; Traupman 104, 353: O.K., fīat or licet

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    The reply to a proposal: Eāmus intrō hinc. — Fīat.

  • placet — agreed, fine by me; placuit, it was agreed, I decided

    impersonal use of placeō · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 911: Placet, pater lepidissime.; Cic. de Or. 1.155: posteā mihi placuit, … ut summōrum ōrātōrum Graecās ōrātiōnēs explicārem

  • Licet. — all right, OK (granting a request)

    impersonal: “it is allowed” · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 1215–1216b; Plaut. Curc. 95b; Traupman 104, 353

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    The yes of someone who agrees to do what is asked: Sed properā. — Licet.

  • Estō. — so be it, all right (conceding)

    future imperative of sum · also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 935; Cic. Fam. 7.18.4: vērum illud estō; Traupman 132

    Grants a point, often before a “but”.

  • per mē licet — I have no objection, as far as I’m concerned it’s allowed

    per with the person who allows it, and licet · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.21: digladientur illī, per mē licet (Lewis & Short s.v. digladior); Caecil. in Cic. Cael. 37: dīde, dīsice, per mē licet (Lewis & Short s.v. disicio); Traupman 105: I have no objection, per mē licet

    “It is allowed as far as I am concerned”: often with a shrug, “let them, for all I care”.

Examples

  • Mē ad cēnam vocā. — Pol vērō vocō. — Eāmus intrō hinc. — Fīat.

    Invite me to dinner. — I certainly do. — Let’s go in, then. — Agreed.Ter. Ph. 1053–1054

  • Fīat, gerātur mōs tibi.

    All right, have it your way.Plaut. Asin. 40

  • Placet, pater lepidissime.

    Agreed, Dad, you’re the best.Ter. Ad. 911

  • Sed properā. — Licet. — Jam hīc fac sit, cēna ut cūrētur. — Licet. — Omnian’ licet? — Licet.

    But hurry. — OK. — See it’s here, so that dinner gets cooked. — OK. — Everything OK? — OK.Plaut. Rud. 1215–1216b

See also agree, suggest, of course.
